state_instruments.blocks: ERCOT large-load interconnection: projects advancing through ERCOT (Batch Zero, loads >=75 MW; community-impact audit >=25 MW) cannot advance pending a PUCT/ERCOT verification audit; no data-center/mining energization approvals until verification completes (SemiAnalysis: 17 facilities / 6.6 GW waiting). Batch Zero studied-load MW allocation study (scheduled Sep-2-2026 to Apr-9-2027) is paused — ERCOT's Seely: 'We will not have the study done by April 9, 2027'.
state_instruments.end_reasoning: Under Abbott the end trigger was the audit: ERCOT verification report targeted Dec-10-2026, PUCT review Dec-17 (SemiAnalysis 09-15) — 'does not by itself reopen permitting' (SemiAnalysis 11-01; WFS 11-04). Hinojosa (sworn in Jan-19-2027) pledged a ban on ALL data-center approvals until the Legislature passes protections. Session Jan-12 to May-31-2027; bills without a two-thirds vote in both chambers take effect Sep-1 (FundaAI 11-04) → base Sep-27 (she keeps the hold until the law applies, so projects approved Jun-Aug don't escape the new rules — inferred). Short case Jun-27 = lifted on passage/signature ('through the 2027 session', WFS 11-04; SemiAnalysis ~8 months). Stress Dec-27 (inferred): the Senate stays Republican (~19-12, Luminix 11-05), a bill can die at sine die → special session (max 30 days) in summer/fall; special-session laws take effect ~91 days after adjournment without two-thirds → late 2027. Independently of politics, studied-load MW allocation will not finish before Apr-2027.
state_instruments.grandfathering: Already-energized loads unaffected. Base Load (executed IA, valid studies, hard commitments) is 'modeled but not re-evaluated' but still needs attestation verification before energization (SemiAnalysis 09-15). Whether Hinojosa's ban reaches already-classified Base Load is not stated — FundaAI's main swing factor (filed applications could resume in 1H27 in its base). Open question: Abbott could release verified Base Load between Dec-17 and Jan-19 (no source either way). Islanded BTM projects are outside ERCOT's scope but are caught by the TCEQ freeze.

state_instruments.blocks: Issuance of ALL TCEQ permits sought by data-center projects — air (NSR/standard permits for on-site generation and gensets), water quality, stormwater, water rights — new AND in-process applications; no MW threshold; no exception for on-site/BTM generation or non-ERCOT areas. Site prep/shell work can proceed, but covered generating equipment and foundations can't be built without the air authorization; missing stormwater authorization blocks land-disturbing work even earlier (SemiAnalysis 11-01).
state_instruments.end_reasoning: Same as TX-ERCOT: Abbott tied it to completion of the ERCOT (and TWDB water) audits, report ~Dec-10-2026; Hinojosa keeps approvals on hold until laws pass (session to May-31, effective Sep-1 without two-thirds) → base Sep-27; short Jun-27 (WFS 'through the 2027 session'); stress Dec-27 (inferred, special session). Ontiveros (SemiAnalysis Ep. 043, podcast, pre-result): air-permit pause 'perhaps mid 2027'. After reopening, the ~12-month on-site plant build follows (deck).
state_instruments.grandfathering: Permits already issued before 2026-09-21 protect the work they authorize, but a campus still needs approval for its next power phase (SemiAnalysis 11-01). TCEQ later suspended ~16-17 permits issued after Sep-21 and shut its STEERS filing portal (Luminix 11-05, secondary; Public Citizen flagged errant approvals per KFOX 11-04). Treatment of renewals/amendments/PBR registrations not specified (B&D alert).

state_instruments.blocks: No pause. state_instruments.end_reasoning: Standing conditions; loss of expedited permitting lengthens state reviews by an unquantified amount. DEQ rule proposals due ~Mar-2027 (180 days).
state_instruments.grandfathering: Existing NDA commitments preserved; programme exclusions apply to new assistance.

Stress: enacted as filed → Jul-27 to Jul-30 (deck: +3.5-3.9 GW pushed to 2031+).

state_instruments.blocks: Pledged temporary statewide pause on state approvals for NEW data centers / 'new construction' until consumer protections exist. Mechanism not stated; likely levers are EPD permits (air for gensets/on-site generation, water withdrawal, NPDES) — inference. Grid terms sit with the separately elected PSC (now 3-2 Democratic), which controls Georgia Power tariffs and large-load contracts.

Base: pause until statutory protections take effect → Jul-27 (~6 months). Stress: Senate stays Republican (29-27 per Luminix) and blocks → pause runs ~12 months to Jan-28 (next session). Deck uses 6 (base) / 12 (stress) on slide 3 but 'Jan-27 to Jan-28' on slide 2.
